We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network.

About the Department - Program 


Join Monash Health as a Quality Systems & Insights Analyst and play a key role in improving the safety and quality of care for one of Victoria's largest health services. Combining data analytics, quality systems expertise and clinical governance insight, you'll transform information into meaningful action, support organisation wide quality systems, and help leaders make decisions that improve patient outcomes. If you enjoy solving problems, working with data, optimising systems, and partnering with stakeholders to drive continuous improvement and positive change, this is an opportunity to make a real impact across a complex and dynamic healthcare environment.


The Quality & Clinical Governance Unit plays a central role in supporting Monash Health's commitment to delivering safe, effective and high-quality care. The team provides leadership, systems and oversight that strengthen clinical governance, quality improvement, patient safety and organisational learning across the health service.


The Quality Insights & Systems team manages and optimises key quality systems, supports the collection and analysis of clinical governance information, and provides meaningful insights that help leaders identify risks, monitor performance and drive continuous improvement. Working collaboratively with programs and services across Monash Health, the team supports evidence-based decision-making and initiatives that enhance patient outcomes and organisational performance.







About the Role 








This is a part time ongoing position located at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, you will work under the leadership of the Quality Insights & Systems manager and collaborate closely with the broader Quality & Clinical Governance team and stakeholders across Monash Health.


This is an exciting opportunity for a quality systems and data professional who enjoys combining analytical thinking, systems administration and continuous improvement to support safer patient care. The role is responsible for maintaining and optimising key organisational quality systems while developing meaningful clinical governance insights that inform decision-making and improvement initiatives.










Key responsibilities include:



Administering and optimising Monash Health's quality systems, including incident management, document control and audit platforms.


Analysing clinical quality data and other information sources to identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement. 


Developing and delivering clinical governance reports, dashboards and insights that support leaders and teams. 


Providing user support, education and training to improve staff capability in quality systems and data interpretation. 


Working with internal stakeholders, external vendors and partner teams to enhance system performance, data integrity and governance processes. 


Contributing to quality improvement initiatives, system enhancements and process optimisation projects.









This role will involve working with stakeholders across multiple Monash Health sites. A hybrid working arrangement may be available in line with team and organisational requirements.







About You 


To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring demonstrated experience in systems administration, data analysis and quality improvement within a complex organisational environment. 


You will be someone who is curious, analytical and solutions-focused, with the ability to translate data into meaningful insights and build strong collaborative relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.


You will have:




Experience administering, supporting or improving systems and processes in a complex organisation. 


Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends and communicate actionable insights. 


Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including report writing, presentations and development of guidance materials.


Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship-building capabilities. 


Experience providing education, training and support to end-users.


High attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining data integrity and quality. 


Demonstrated problem-solving skills and a continuous improvement mindset. 


Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.


Experience using RiskMan, PROMPT, MARS or similar systems will be highly regarded.



Mandatory Requirements:




Degree qualification in health, quality, business management, data analytics or a related discipline.


Current right to work in Australia. 


Ability to obtain and maintain required screening checks, including National Police Check and Working with Children Check.


Current Victorian Driver's Licence is highly desirable



 
Desirable:




Knowledge of quality, safety and clinical governance principles within a health service environment. 


Experience working in a complex healthcare organisation.This role offers the opportunity to contribute directly to Monash Health's quality and safety agenda, helping to strengthen systems, generate valuable organisational insights and support continuous improvement across one of Australia's largest health services.

We'relooking for aSenior Business Analystfor a fixed-term opportunity within our Digital and Technology team, supporting Anglicare's Integration Management Office (IMO) IT Workstream. Vacancy Listing Dates 2/07/2026 to 30/07/2026
Please Quote Reference Number 17401
- Seeking an Organisation and Methods (Quality Classing) Analyst
- Salary $80,000 + superannuation
- Join Australian Food and Fibre

Australian Food & Fibre (AFF) is a modern, integrated business that combines significant knowledge and expertise to supply quality Australian cotton to the world, as well as cereals, pulses and oil seeds.

We have a career opportunity for a skilled Organisation & Methods (Quality Classing) Analyst to join our team in our Artarmon laboratory, 2064, New South Wales.

Overall Responsibilities:

At the Australian Food & Fibre, Artarmon, facility you are responsible for testing, evaluating and grading our agricultural commodities. They ensure that raw materials (primarily cotton) meet strict domestic and international quality standards before they are exported or sold.

Daily tasks:
- Fibre testing - operating specialised laboratory instruments to analyse the physical properties of cotton samples. This includes measuring fibre length, strength, micronaire (fineness), maturity, and colour.
- Assess current systems - analyse and evaluate capabilities, and workflows to identify bottlenecks and process gaps.
- Commodity grading - applying standardised classing rules to assign grades to cotton lint. This determines the market value and spinning utility of the crop.
- Sample management - preparing, tracking, and cataloguing physical samples sent from various AFF farming and ginning operations (such as their sites in Moree and Narrabri).
- Data Analysis - recording and verifying data within classing and laboratory software systems, ensuring that every batch meets the requirements of export contracts.
- Quality assurance - monitoring laboratory equipment calibration to ensure accurate and reliable test results.
- Classing and compliance - develop, maintain and enforce Quality Auditor standards, reviewing operating procedures and advising on any departures from established guidelines.

Our ideal candidate will have:
- Hands-on trade experience through on-the-job training OR Certificate III in Cotton Ginning OR specialised industry-recognised classing grader advantageous OR an IT background will better equip you with the analytical skills required in our laboratory and for this role.
- Minimum 2+ years of experience in procedural/business/computer analysis, continuous improvement or quality control
- A Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business, IT, Commerce, Operations Management or a related field will be highly regarded.

While a formal agricultural degree can be advantageous for career advancement with us, our hands-on approach for you to function well in the role is to assist you in gaining certification from Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry as part of your induction with us and a requirement for our quality control and cotton exporting criteria.

In return, we can offer:
- Highly competitive salary package ($80,000 + super)
- Excellent professional development and career progression opportunities.
- Supportive, dynamic team environment with hybrid working arrangements.
- Opportunities for ongoing employment and training across seasonal operations.
- Contribution to the local agricultural economy in our regional NSW operations.

Join our company and enjoy a supportive, family-friendly environment where you'll receive in-house assistance and continuous opportunities for up-skilling, ensuring your ongoing professional growth.

Do you want a career that means more? At Anglicare Sydney, we bring the strength, the support and the strategy to make it happen. 

For over 170 years, Anglicare has supported people and communities across Sydney and the surrounds. Our Seniors Communities portfolio spans Retirement Living and Support at Home services, supporting thousands of older Australians and their families. 

We'relooking for aCyber Risk Analystto join our Cyber Security and IT Risk team. This role focuses on performing cyber risk assessments, supporting governance and compliance initiatives, and helping strengthen Anglicare's security posture across people,processesand technology. Workingwith the Cyber Risk and Threat team and their processes, you will helpidentifyand mitigate cyberrisks, andcontribute to the protection of Anglicare's critical systems and digital assets.

As part of a purpose-driven organisation, you'll be working in a collaborative and values-led environment where your work directly contributes to enriching lives and strengthening communities. 

Your opportunity

The Cyber Risk Analyst playsan important rolein supporting Anglicare's cyber security governance, riskmanagementand compliance activities. You will work across the organisation to conduct risk assessments,monitorcompliance with security frameworks and policies, and provide insights that help strengthen cyber resilience and reduce organisational risk. 

Working with the Cyber Risk & Threat team,you will collaborate with Cyber Security, ITArchitectureand business stakeholders to support governance frameworks, threat modellingactivitiesand risk mitigation programs. Through your work, you will help ensure Anglicaremaintainsa secure and resilient technology environment that supports its mission and operations.

With ownership, you will:

Conduct cyber security, operational and compliance risk assessments toidentifyrisks,vulnerabilitiesand areas for improvement. You will support riskaudit activitiesandrisk mitigationas well asmonitor compliance with security policies and standardsacross the organisation. You willassistwith threat modellingand risk mitigation activities, whileworking with the team in accordancetotheir processes,toproducehigh-quality reports and documentation that support informed decision-making and strong cyber security governance outcomes.

What you'll bring

You are a cyber security and risk professional with experience in governance,complianceand risk management practices. You have a strong understanding of cyber security principles, risk assessmentmethodologiesand industry frameworks, and enjoyidentifyingrisks andworking with teamstomitigate issuesthat improve organisational security and resilience.

You combine strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to communicate complex concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You are collaborative, detail-orientedand proactive, with a passion for continuous learning and staying informed aboutemergingthreats, evolving regulations and industry best practices.

You will also need:

- Tertiary qualification in Information Technology, Cyber Security, RiskManagementor a related field. Certifications such as CRISC, CISM or ISO 27001 are highly desirable.
- 3+ years' experience in cyber security, risk management,governanceor compliance-related roles.
- Experience conducting risk assessments, supporting risk mitigationinitiativesand contributing to governance programs.
- Knowledge of cyber security and governance frameworks such as SCF, NIST and ISO 27001.
- Understanding of Australian regulatory and compliance requirements and industry standards.
- Experience with threat modelling and secure design principles.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and risk assessment capabilities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Strong documentation and reporting skills with attention to detail.
- Proven ability to collaborate effectively across teams and contribute to organisation-wide cyber security initiatives.

Why Anglicare?

At Anglicare, we provide meaningful opportunities and choice - both for the communities we support and the people who work with us. 

Here'swhatyou'llenjoy: 

Flexible work options to balance life and career. 

Salary packaging benefits - up to $15,900 of your income tax free, plus $2,650 for meals and entertainment.

Belonging to a supportive, purpose-driven team committed to making a difference.

All applicants will receive a response. Anglicare is as wonderfully diverse as the communities we serve. While guided by our Christian values, our team includes people of all faiths and backgrounds.

We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and people of all ages, genders,abilitiesand cultural backgrounds.
